title: Book Three · Chapter 35: The Other Time
story:
Two weeks later, Mum takes out her work sheet on Sunday.

“Next Saturday,” she says. “I need to leave before ten. The customer will try her coat on at home.”

Ronan looks up from his book.

“And the rice comes that morning,” she adds. “Can you be here for it?”

“Yes.”

He says it quickly. Then he remembers the track.

“What time?”

“Between ten and eleven.”

Ronan puts his book down. He opens his notebook to the running day.

“Anna starts at eleven. I said I would be there at half past ten.”

Mum looks at the two times.

“Your father works all morning. I can't leave the customer halfway through the fitting.”

Mum has already checked the time with her customer. The woman needs to try the coat over her usual clothes. The job will take more than one quick look at a sleeve. There may be a second try before Mum can leave.

“Can the man bring the rice earlier?”

“You can ask. He has other people to visit too.”

Ronan walks to the rice shop after lunch. The owner knows the order. It is one large bag for the family.

“West Lane, next Saturday,” the man says.

“Can you come before ten?”

The man shakes his head.

“I collect the bags first. Then I bring them round. Between ten and eleven.”

“Will we be the first house?”

“I can't promise that.”

Ronan looks at the bags behind the counter. The man has several names on a sheet. His home is only one stop.

“All right,” Ronan says.

He walks back slowly. The school is about twenty minutes from home on foot. If the rice comes at eleven, Anna may finish before he gets there.

At the crossing, he waits behind two carts. A few minutes pass before he can cross. On Saturday, that part will still need time.

At the green door, he stops beside his bike. The old bell shines under the handlebar. The busy corner will still be busy on Saturday.

He does not count the whole road as a fast ride.

Mum is measuring the coat when he comes inside.

“Ten to eleven,” he tells her.

She nods. “We need the bag by the kitchen wall. The man will carry it in. You don't have to lift it.”

Ronan looks at his notebook again. The words half past ten are still on the page.

“I need to tell Anna.”

“Tomorrow?”

“Yes.”

He sits down and writes the delivery time below his own time. Then he crosses out the promise to arrive at half past ten.

Dad comes home later and reads the page.

“You may catch the run,” he says.

“Or miss it.”

Dad nods.

Ronan puts the notebook in his school bag. He wants Anna to know before she makes her own plans for the morning.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

fitting＝试衣、调整衣服尺寸；order＝订购的物品；on foot＝步行；delivery＝送货。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan答应到场的时间和家里的哪项安排发生了冲突？
2. 他有没有得到提前送米的保证？他准备什么时候告诉Anna？

## 读句子

**The man will carry it in.**

拆开看：The man / will carry it / in.

送货的人／会把它搬／搬进来（it指米袋）。
